subject: Re: Export controls, derivative licensing, and SFTP onboarding for LLM outputs
messages:
From: Tom Everett <tom@brightbridge.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Export controls and derivative/licensing questions for LLM outputs

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightBridge is excited about Redwood's latency and the dedicated routing options. Before we move to a trial, our legal and compliance teams asked for clarity on several items related to the data flows and downstream rights:

1) We need a binding no-training commitment for customer-provided prompts/records that contain PHI for customers in our EU region (or, alternatively, an auditable opt-out workflow).
2) We require a way to pull transcripts and model outputs via a secure push or an SFTP pull (EU-hosted) on a regular cadence for our archival/escrow process.
3) For outputs (generated text/attachments), our procurement team wants a limited derivative license (we need to be able to use outputs internally and sublicense to downstream care partners; we cannot accept broad IP assignment). Can you outline licensing language?
4) Any evidence pack you can supply for SOC2 / subprocessor access to show no-training controls and KV cache handling would be helpful.

Can you put together next steps and what configurability we can expect? Procurement (procurement@brightbridge.ai) is copied to coordinate timelines.

Best,
Tom
Tom Everett
Head of Product Security
BrightBridge Health

[Attachment: none]
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Tom Everett <tom@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-21T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Export controls and derivative/licensing questions for LLM outputs

Tom — appreciate the clear list. Closing the loop with legal & compliance here but high level:

- No-train commitment: We offer a contractual no-training (no-LLM-improvement) option scoped to customer-identifiers and datasets. That option comes with operational controls (dedicated routing to a tenant-isolated inference pool, KV/prefix cache isolation, and a suppressed telemetry path). We can put "no-train" language in a DPA addendum and offer audit logs showing model invocation vs telemetry retention.

- SFTP exports: We support scheduled exports to customer SFTP endpoints. For EU residency you can pick an EU SFTP target (we can host a short-term transfer bucket in eu-west if needed). We'll provide an onboarding runbook and an initial 2-week PoC to validate push/pull cadence.

- Derivative licensing: We typically offer a limited, perpetual, non-exclusive license for outputs that allows internal use and redistribution to downstream partners for the customer's business purposes (no assignment of model weights). If you need sublicense rights to care partners, we can capture that in a limited sublicense clause with standard indemnity carveouts — I'll loop in legal for specific wording.

- Evidence pack: I will attach a draft DPA addendum (no-train language included), the SFTP onboarding runbook, and a short escrow proposal. Marissa (legal) and Neha (compliance) are on cc to confirm contractual language and the compliance evidence we can provide.

Proposed next steps:
1) Legal redline: we send DPA addendum draft (attached) — please flag must-haves.
2) Technical PoC: schedule 2-week SFTP export to your EU endpoint + one test dataset.
3) Escrow/derivative path: legal & procurement evaluate the attached escrow proposal.

Attachments: DPA_addendum_no_train_draft_v1.docx; SFTP_onboarding_runbook.pdf; Escrow_proposal_Protexio.pdf

If that plan works, I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_addendum_no_train_draft_v1.docx (docx)]
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Export controls and derivative/licensing questions for LLM outputs

Rafael — quick notes from legal after a first pass on the DPA draft: 

- No-train clause: use explicit scope language — (i) "no use of customer data or derivatives for model training or improvement" and (ii) define exceptions (e.g., aggregated telemetry that is strictly non-identifying with a customer opt-in). Add an audit-rights paragraph (quarterly) limited to metadata and processed-request logs; retention of the audit evidence should be 12 months unless customer requests longer.

- Derivative license: propose this language: "Customer is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and distribute Outputs for its internal business operations and to its downstream contractors and partners solely for the purpose of delivering Customer services; Redwood retains all underlying model and weight IP." Add a clause that derivative sublicenses require notice to Redwood and must comply with privacy obligations.

- Escrow: procurement will want an escrow agreement that enumerates what is escrows (generated outputs, logs) and the release conditions. Recommend Protexio as a vendor; attach a short template.

- SFTP runbook: ops note — for EU SFTP endpoints we should require key-based auth, host-key pinning, and a daily checksum report. Also suggest an optional retention TTL on exported files (default 90 days) unless customer requests otherwise — that reduces our long tail.

Neha, can you confirm what evidence we can provide for KV cache isolation and telemetry suppression? If we can supply an operations playbook snippet and an obfuscated log extract that should satisfy their SOC reviewers.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Tom Everett <tom@brightbridge.ai>, procurement@brightbridge.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-23T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Export controls and derivative/licensing questions for LLM outputs — proposal and next steps

Tom / procurement team — following internal review, here's a concise proposal and immediate next steps so we can get a PoC running this week: 

Proposal highlights:
- Contract: We will provide a DPA addendum with a scoped "no-train" commitment for the datasets you identify (draft attached). The addendum includes quarterly audit rights limited to processed request logs and a 12-month evidence retention baseline.
- Exports: Technical PoC — Redwood will push exports to an EU SFTP endpoint you designate. Auth: key-based + host-key pinning. File TTL: default 90 days (configurable). We'll produce a checksum report and a mapping file that links export batches to request IDs for traceability.
- Derivative license: Perpetual, non-exclusive license for Outputs with limited sublicensing to care partners (see proposed wording in the attached DPA draft). Redwood keeps model IP and weights.
- Escrow: We propose a third-party escrow (Protexio) with the scope limited to outputs and delivery logs; see attached proposal for release criteria.

Attachments: DPA_addendum_no_train_draft_v1.docx; SFTP_onboarding_runbook.pdf; Escrow_proposal_Protexio.pdf

Immediate next steps:
1) Procurement: review the attached escrow proposal and confirm vendor (procurement@brightbridge.ai).
2) Legal: please redline the DPA addendum and return within 3 business days (Tom — if you have a preferred markups list please send).
3) Technical: provide an EU SFTP endpoint and test account (we recommend a short-lived key pair). We can stand up the PoC export within 48 hours of receiving credentials.

If that aligns with you, I'll send a calendar invite for a kickoff and include our SRE lead for the export configuration.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting the PoC running.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SFTP_onboarding_runbook.pdf (pdf)]
